e: Progesterone ↑es central respiratory drive → hyperventilation in pregnancy.
↓es renal perfusion pressure → ↑es renin release from JG cells (baroreceptor-mediated).
Photoreceptors are unique among sensory receptors in hyperpolarizing (not depolarizing) on stimulation by light.
Dentate gyrus of the hippocampus is a recognised site of adult neurogenesis.
The negatively-charged glomerular basement membrane repels anions → cations filtered most readily at a given radius.
SGLT1 co-transports Na⁺ c̅ glucose, driving water absorption independent of the defective CFTR channel — the basis of oral rehydration therapy.

RCA flow is biphasic (systole + diastole) since RV pressure stays low throughout the cycle.
LCA flow is mainly diastolic, as high LV systolic pressure compresses intramural vessels.
Damaged glomerular filtration barrier → proteinuria (albumin leaks into urine).

Thick ascending limb (NKCC2) actively pumps out NaCl but is water-impermeable → counter-current multiplier.
Vasa recta = counter-current exchanger.

Insulin ↑es GLUT4 translocation in skeletal muscle (and adipose).
Liver uses GLUT2, which is insulin-independent.
Exogenous testosterone → negative feedback on hypothalamus/pituitary → LH ↓es and FSH ↓es.
Pacinian corpuscle = onion-like lamellated encapsulated ending in the deep dermis; senses vibration and deep pressure.
Intercalated disc = fascia adherens (cadherins) + desmosomes + gap junctions; tight junctions are absent.

Insulin ↑es protein synthesis and ↓es blood glucose; epinephrine ↑es glycogenolysis; glucagon ↑es gluconeogenesis.
Thyroxine ↑es (not ↓es) BMR.
Saliva is hypotonic – lowest Na⁺ among GI secretions.

Serotonin is synthesised in the raphe nuclei.
DA – substantia nigra/VTA; NE – locus ceruleus; ACh – nucleus basalis of Meynert.
2025 Nobel (Physiology/Medicine): discovery of peripheral immune tolerance (regulatory T cells, FOXP3).
Arcuate nucleus (NPY/AgRP & POMC neurons) is the primary leptin target – site of leptin resistance.
Isovolumetric contraction: all valves closed → pressure ↑es c̅ constant volume.
Inspiration ↑es venous return to RV and pools blood in lungs → transient ↓ LV filling → SBP dips slightly.

MG: ↓ functional postsynaptic AChRs → safety factor falls → decremental response on RNS.
Lambert-Eaton (presynaptic VGCC) → incremental.
Diabetic OGTT: fasting ≥126 mg/dL and 2-h value ≥200 mg/dL – curves B and D.
P-glycoprotein (ABC family): ATP-driven efflux pump – primary active transport.
Kidney (renal reabsorption, mainly thick ascending limb) is the main regulator of Mg²⁺ balance.

Kidney (urine output) adjusts volume, osmolality & electrolytes over the long term.
RR, SpO₂, HR = short-term responses.
↑ Peripheral resistance (afterload) → ↑ peak pressure, ↓ stroke volume (tall, narrow loop).
Hypoxia → hyperventilation → CO₂ ↓es → respiratory alkalosis (renal HCO₃⁻ excretion compensates).
IGF-1/2 are structurally most similar to proinsulin (~50% homology; they retain the C-peptide-like domain), not mature insulin.
Surface tension ↑es on inspiration (alveoli expand, surfactant spreads thin); ↓es on expiration as surfactant is concentrated.
Bezold-Jarisch reflex: bradycardia + hypotension + apnoea/hypopnoea (vagal); tachycardia is not part of it.
Alpha waves (8-13 Hz, occipital) are blocked on eye opening (alpha blockade).
Tetanizing frequency = 1/contraction period = 1/0.04 s = 25 Hz (latent period is not used)
Feed-forward = body reacts before the change happens.\nSkin cooling → vasoconstriction starts before core temp falls. \nTemp regulation (D) = both feed-forward + feedback.
Fever: pyrogens/PGE₂ raise the set point in the pre-optic nucleus (anterior hypothalamus).
ADH acts on V2 receptors → ↑es AQP2 (water) and urea absorption in the collecting duct.\nThin ascending limb is passive and ADH has no effect there.
Tight junctions (zonula occludens) are apicolateral: at the apical end of the lateral membrane.
